about: Vaultleaf change log. Append new entries at the end, oldest first, and never reorder or remove them: people's What's new depends on the order. type: added, improved, changed, fixed or security. audience: everyone, or admin for changes only site admins need to know. Changes nobody wrote an entry for are logged automatically in changelog-auto.json.

entries.title: Project set up
entries.text: Vaultleaf's folder was created in the c3jumpw/public repository with a new Vercel project, ready for the first release.

entries.title: Vaultleaf launches
entries.text: An encrypted password vault that unlocks with your master password, then a passcode. A recovery key gets you back in if you forget them. Everything is encrypted on your device before it's saved.

entries.title: Classic notes view and Modern cards
entries.text: Read accounts like the notes you keep passwords in now, one detail per line, or as cards with copy buttons. Write an account as a plain note and Vaultleaf turns the lines into fields.

entries.title: Everything an account needs
entries.text: Passwords, PINs, API keys, secret phrases, 2FA codes, security questions with hidden answers, the account's admin users and their emails, the tool and account name, the date stored and notes.

entries.title: History and copy records
entries.text: Each account keeps every change, the old passwords and keys it replaced, and the date and time of every copy.

entries.title: Labels, sub-labels and search
entries.text: Group accounts with labels like folders, nest them as sub-labels, and search names, usernames, emails, websites, labels and notes.

entries.title: Import from Notes or a CSV file
entries.text: Paste your notes, many at once, or bring a CSV export from a browser or another password manager.

entries.title: Generator, Health and Activity
entries.text: Make strong passwords and passphrases, see weak, reused and overdue passwords, and review every copy and change across all accounts.

entries.title: Backups, restore and Recently deleted
entries.text: Save an encrypted backup file and restore it on any device. Deleted accounts stay in Recently deleted for 30 days.

entries.title: Illustrated guide
entries.text: A guide with pictures of every screen, inside Vaultleaf and on its own page.

entries.title: Published on Vercel
entries.text: Live at public-vault-leaf.vercel.app with strict security headers, offline use and home-screen install. Only people signed in to the Vercel team could open it.

entries.title: Moved to the c3jumpw/mco repository
entries.text: The code moved to the vault-leaf folder of c3jumpw/mco. The Vercel project was renamed mco-vault-leaf and the address became mco-vault-leaf.vercel.app. Vaults saved at the earlier address stayed there.

entries.title: Sync between devices
entries.text: Turn on sync and enter your sync code on your other devices. Only encrypted data is uploaded, and edits on two devices are combined.

entries.title: Sync storage in Supabase
entries.text: Synced vaults are stored encrypted in the MKC-Admin Supabase project, in the vaultleaf_vaults and vaultleaf_blobs tables.

entries.title: Face ID and fingerprint unlock
entries.text: Turn it on in Settings to unlock without typing. Your password and passcode are still asked for every 14 days.

entries.title: Leaked password check
entries.text: Health can check your passwords against public breach lists. Only 5 characters of a scrambled fingerprint are sent, never the password.

entries.title: Attach files
entries.text: Keep ID scans, recovery sheets and short PDFs on the account they belong to, encrypted, up to 5 MB each.

entries.title: Emergency kits
entries.text: Make a file with everything, or only some labels, that a trusted person opens with its own code.

entries.title: Guided tour
entries.text: A step-by-step tour of every feature with real screenshots. Find it in Settings and on the Guide page.

entries.title: Admin tour
entries.text: Eight steps on running the site: who can open it, publishing and rolling back, sync storage, and helping people who are locked out or changing devices.

entries.title: Docs refresh themselves
entries.text: Every push to main that changes Vaultleaf retakes the screenshots and rebuilds the tour and guide, and fails if a feature has no tour step or guide section.

entries.title: What's new after each update
entries.text: The first time you unlock after an update, you see what changed, with pictures. You only see changes that apply to you.

entries.title: Choose your role
entries.text: In Settings, say whether you run the Vaultleaf site. Admins get the Admin page and hear about admin changes. It doesn't open anyone else's vault.

entries.title: Admin page with the change log
entries.text: Every change since launch, oldest first, with filters and downloads as JSON, CSV or Markdown. Find it under Admin.

entries.title: The change log keeps itself up to date
entries.text: Every push that changes Vaultleaf is logged automatically. Changes people should hear about get a written entry, which also shows in their What's new.

entries.title: New address: vaultleaf.mkcworkspace.com
entries.text: Vaultleaf is moving to vaultleaf.mkcworkspace.com. Your vault doesn't move by itself. When the new address is ready, a banner here walks you through bringing it over with your sync code or a backup.

entries.title: Who can open the new address
entries.text: Vercel Authentication covers the vercel.app addresses only. vaultleaf.mkcworkspace.com opens for anyone with the link, and each visitor gets their own empty, private vault. To require Vercel sign-in there too, change Deployment Protection to cover all deployments.
